headers.//: THE ROOT URL. Header globs match the REQUEST PATH, not the file finally served: a request for '/' contains no '.html', so the rule below never fires for it and Firebase's default max-age=3600 applies. That is exactly the stale-index.html trap this migration exists to close — the root is the one URL everybody actually visits, and index.html is what carries every ?v= cache-bust. Verified with curl after deploy; do not remove.

Code + config: always revalidate. no-cache still CACHES — it just never serves a stale copy without asking (a 304 costs one conditional request, not a re-download). This is what ends the stale-file fights; the ?v= query strings are now belt-and-braces.
The service worker must never be served stale, or a bad worker sticks around.
Static assets never change in place — a new icon means a new filename — so cache them hard.
